assumptions.note: Share of nominal private consumption (gross of VAT) by VAT rate category. Keys map to parameters: standard -> vat_rate_standard, reduced1 -> vat_rate_reduced1, reduced2 -> vat_rate_reduced2, zero -> 0% / exempt (no output VAT).  rough split; should come from MF/GUS data on consumption by VAT rate.

VAT compliance gap as a fraction of theoretical revenue.  order of magnitude only; replace with the latest VAT gap estimate for Poland (e.g. the European Commission VAT Gap report) after verification.
Price elasticity of real consumption demand w.r.t. the consumer price (gross of VAT). Assumes full pass-through of VAT changes to consumer prices.  illustrative value, no literature source verified.
Share of the CIT tax base attributable to small taxpayers (9% rate).  should come from MF CIT-8 aggregate statistics.

Default taxable-income distribution of taxpayers on the tax scale (skala podatkowa), as (mean annual taxable income in zł, number of taxpayers in millions) per group.  synthetic distribution shaped to look plausible; should be replaced by MF "Informacja dotycząca rozliczenia podatku dochodowego od osób fizycznych" bracket data once loaded.

Split of non-agricultural business income by taxation form (shares sum to 1). scale -> taxed on the scale together with wages, flat -> pit_flat_rate, lump -> pit_lump_rate_default applied to revenue (see PIT_LUMP_REVENUE_TO_INCOME).  rough split.

Split of non-agricultural business income by taxation form (shares sum to 1). scale -> taxed on the scale together with wages, flat -> pit_flat_rate, lump -> pit_lump_rate_default applied to revenue (see PIT_LUMP_REVENUE_TO_INCOME).  rough split.

Split of non-agricultural business income by taxation form (shares sum to 1). scale -> taxed on the scale together with wages, flat -> pit_flat_rate, lump -> pit_lump_rate_default applied to revenue (see PIT_LUMP_REVENUE_TO_INCOME).  rough split.
Ratio of recorded revenue (ryczałt base) to income for lump-sum taxpayers.  illustrative value.

Non-agricultural business income (PIT base outside wages) as a ratio to the wage bill. No business-income series is loaded, so the projection ties it to the wage bill.  illustrative ratio; should come from MF PIT statistics.
Marginal propensity to consume out of disposable income: a PIT change of dT (mld zł) moves nominal consumption by -HOUSEHOLD_MPC * dT.  illustrative value, no literature source verified.

Share of private consumption in GDP: a relative change of real consumption x moves real GDP by CONSUMPTION_GDP_SHARE * x (no import leakage or offsets modelled).  order of magnitude only; should come from GUS national accounts.
Elasticity of employment w.r.t. real GDP (short-run, Okun-type).  illustrative value, no literature source verified.
Number of most recent years used for the per-tax calibration factors (mean ratio of recorded revenue to module output at current law). Method choice, not a data value.

Structural breaks: series -> first year recorded under new rules. Years >= the break are not used for calibration or scored by the backtest. rev_pit: from 2025 the state budget keeps a much smaller PIT share (local-government financing reform), 2024 97.6 -> 2025 28.75 mld zł (MF reports).
VAT liczony od konsumpcji w cenach bazowych skorygowanej tylko o zmianę dochodu rozporządzalnego z PIT; reakcję wolumenu na stawki VAT liczy wyłącznie moduł VAT (bez podwójnego liczenia).
Druga runda w jednym kroku: zmiana VAT/PIT -> ceny i dochód rozporządzalny -> konsumpcja (i baza VAT), PKB, zatrudnienie -> bazy PIT i CIT.
Nominalne wynagrodzenie nie reaguje na zmiany podatków (brak sprzężenia płacowo-cenowego w v1).
Nadwyżka operacyjna brutto rośnie jak realny PKB x CPI od ostatniego roku danych.
Kalibracja liczy lata historyczne przy obecnym prawie (domyślne parametry), nie przy prawie obowiązującym w danym roku.
PIT w budżecie państwa: zmiana zasad podziału od 2025 r. (reforma finansowania JST); kalibracja do 2024; wykonanie 2025 nie jest porównywalne z prognozą przy dotychczasowych zasadach.
